title: The GCN layer
blurb: Neighbourhood aggregation, W and B, k hops

hook.title: Gossip at a party
hook.text: At a party everyone holds an opinion. In each round, each person forms a new opinion by **averaging their friends’ opinions** (run through a little thinking step) and mixing in a dose of their own conviction. After one round you've heard from your friends; after two, from friends-of-friends; after $k$ rounds, from everyone within $k$ handshakes.
hook.recall: Remember the gossip: each round = average the friends, transform, mix in yourself. After $k$ rounds you’ve heard from everyone within $k$ hops.

explore.intro: The GCN layer $h_v^{(k+1)}=\sigma\big(W_k\sum_{u\in N(v)}\frac{h_u^{(k)}}{|N(v)|}+B_kh_v^{(k)}\big)$ on a 6-node graph with 2-D features. $W,B$ are scalars here.
tasks: Select node D (one neighbour) and step $k$ from 1 to 3. Watch the yellow receptive field grow.
Set $W=1,B=0$ with no non-linearity. What does a layer do to node B?
explore.takeaway: Layer-0 embedding = input feature. A layer averages neighbours’ previous embeddings (transformed by $W_k$), adds $B_kh_v^{(k)}$ and applies a non-linearity. After $k$ layers a node sees its $k$-hop neighbourhood.

build.prompt: Order the computation of one GCN layer for node $v$.
items: Take the previous-layer embeddings of the neighbours $u\in N(v)$
build.explanation: Slide 17–18: average information from neighbours, then apply a neural network; the formula is $\sigma(W_k\sum h_u/|N(v)|+B_kh_v)$.

questions.prompt: Take the slide’s example: node B has neighbours A and C. Scalar embeddings $h_A^0=2$, $h_C^0=4$, $h_B^0=1$; $W_0=1$, $B_0=0.5$; ignore the non-linearity. Compute $h_B^1=W_0\frac{h_A^0+h_C^0}{2}+B_0h_B^0$.
The layer-$k$ embedding of a node carries information from nodes how far away?
options: Nodes at distance exactly 1 and $k$ only

questions.explanation: Slide 16: layer-0 embedding of node $v$ is its input feature.

questions.prompt: Path graph $v - a - b - c - d$. After **2** GCN layers, the embedding of $v$ depends on the input features of:
Which statement about the GCN layer is FALSE?
options: $B_k$ transforms the node’s own hidden vector
The summation over neighbours is a permutation-invariant aggregation
The summation over neighbours depends on the order in which neighbours are listed
questions.explanation: “Notice summation is a permutation invariant pooling/aggregation.”

questions.prompt: *“A 2-layer GCN lets node A see only its direct neighbours.”* What’s wrong?
options: After two layers A’s embedding contains information from nodes up to **2 hops** away (neighbours of neighbours)
A 2-layer GCN sees the entire graph always
questions.explanation: Round 2 of gossip carries friends-of-friends’ opinions.
